contract.schema: rms_norm_dynamic_per_token_fp8(Tensor(a!) result, Tensor input, Tensor weight, Tensor(b!) scale, float epsilon, Tensor? scale_ub=None, Tensor(c!)? residual=None) -> ()
contract.inputs: contiguous F32, FP16, or BF16 input and weight; optional same-shape, same-dtype mutable residual
contract.output: caller-owned FP8 E4M3FN result plus one caller-owned F32 scale per flattened row
contract.residual: when present, raw F32 input+residual sums drive all three passes and the storage-dtype-rounded sums are written to residual during the final pass
contract.scale_upper_bound: rejected; the registered vLLM dynamic per-token FP8 fusion passes None
contract.aliasing: input, weight, output, scales, and optional residual must be pairwise disjoint at the checked bridge
contract.gemm_boundary: unchanged vLLM Cutlass FP8 scaled-mm; Loom owns only Add+RMSNorm+dynamic FP8 preparation

implementation.path: PyTorch -> boxed Stable ABI dispatcher -> checked ABI9 Rust bridge -> safe Rust dispatch -> handwritten CUDA
implementation.description: RMS reduction, normalized weighted absmax reduction, then residual store plus FP8 quantization
implementation.specialization: separate compile-time kernels for optional residual and vectorized/scalar storage
implementation.vectorization: four input, weight, and residual elements plus four FP8 output bytes per aligned pack
implementation.vllm_registration: both plain RMSNorm and fused Add+RMSNorm dynamic per-token FP8 fusion keys map to the exact Loom schema

direct_named_baseline.protocol: BF16 hidden size 896, same preallocated Stable ABI operator boundary, 0.5 second GEMM warm-up per provider, 100 warm-ups, 10 samples, 2000 launches per sample, provider-order reversal
direct_named_baseline.replay_stability: residual cases use zero input and random residual so repeated in-place eager and CUDA Graph calls preserve the residual without timing a reset copy
direct_named_baseline.correctness: every Loom FP8 byte, scale, and optional residual byte matches vLLM
direct_named_baseline.interpretation: The direct advantage is order-stable: 2.9-12.3% by eager dispatch and 3.3-8.2% under CUDA Graph replay across the measured cases.

configuration.provider_isolation: fresh process and distinct vLLM/TorchInductor cache root per provider

prefill_only.interpretation: All six order-reversed prefill cases improve. The narrow qualified batch-latency range is 1.0066-1.0506x.

prefill_plus_decode.interpretation: Batch latency and TPOT cross parity after provider-order reversal. No decode, TPOT, or throughput acceleration is claimed.

decision: Accept the first K2.5 quantization-plumbing slice for the exact optional-residual RMSNorm-to-dynamic-FP8 boundary. It has an order-stable direct advantage and a narrow order-stable Qwen2.5 prefill win while leaving Cutlass GEMM unchanged. Keep the adapter opt-in and make no decode-throughput claim.
